SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
